The decorator answered with a redirect to `LOGIN_URL`, `"/accounts/login/"` by default, with the page asked for in `"next"` (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:user_passes_test`).
On the way out the session middleware saw a changed session and saved it, and set the cookie `"sessionid"` to the key, for two weeks and with HttpOnly (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`).

`SessionMiddleware.process_request` reads the key from the request's cookie and makes a session store for it, of the class called `SessionStore` in the module that `SESSION_ENGINE` names, `django.contrib.sessions.backends.db` unless it names another; the middleware imports that module once, when it is made (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware`).

It records that it was **accessed**, and, when a key is set or deleted, that it was **modified** ([The session store: `SessionBase`](auth/sessions.md)) (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._get_session`).

And a response whose session was accessed gets `"Cookie"` in its `"Vary"`, since what it says may depend on who asked ([`SessionMiddleware`: the cookie and the save](auth/session-middleware.md)) (`django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:SessionMiddleware.process_response`).

Its data is a dictionary, serialized as JSON unless `SESSION_SERIALIZER` names another serializer; the default store keeps it signed, and compressed when that is shorter by more than one byte: a row whose data no longer matches its signature loads as an empty session (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.encode`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.decode`).

Whenever the search ends with no user, the `user_login_failed` signal is sent ([Authenticating: `authenticate` and the backends](auth/authenticating.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:authenticate`).

When no user has that username it hashes the password all the same, so that the time a refusal takes does not tell an existing username from a missing one (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:check_password_with_timing_attack_mitigation`).

It then puts the user on the request, replaces the CSRF secret, and sends `user_logged_in`, whose receiver, connected when the user model has a `last_login` field, records the time there ([The user of a request: `login`, `logout` and `AuthenticationMiddleware`](auth/login.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:login`, `docs/topics/http/sessions.txt`).

It puts on the request a `SimpleLazyObject` that calls `django.contrib.auth.get_user` the first time the user is used, and keeps the answer for the rest of the request ([Lazy objects: `LazyObject` and `SimpleLazyObject`](utils/lazy-objects.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/middleware.py:AuthenticationMiddleware.process_request`).

So changing a password logs out every session of that user, which the documentation names as the purpose; the password change view keeps its own session with `update_session_auth_hash` (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`, `docs/topics/auth/default.txt`).

`logout` sends `user_logged_out` first, so that its receivers can still tell who it was, then flushes the session (the data emptied, the stored session deleted, the key dropped) and puts an `AnonymousUser` on the request (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:logout`).

For anyone else it asks each backend in turn, until one says yes or raises `PermissionDenied`, which makes the answer no (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:_user_has_perm`).

`ModelBackend` builds the set of a user's permissions, the user's own and the user's groups', in two queries, keeps it on the user object, and answers from the set; an inactive user has none, and a question about one object gets an empty set from it, its permissions being by model and not by object, as `Permission`'s docstring says ([Permissions: `Permission`, groups and `has_perm`](auth/permissions.md)) (`django/contrib/auth/backends.py:ModelBackend._get_permissions`).
The view's `django.contrib.messages.api.success` is `add_message` at the level `SUCCESS`, 25 (`django/contrib/messages/constants.py`).

It hands the message to the storage that `MessageMiddleware` put on the request, which queues it if its level is at least `MESSAGE_LEVEL`, `INFO` (20) unless the setting says otherwise (`django/contrib/messages/api.py:add_message`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage.add`).

In the other order there would be no session when the storage is made, and `SessionStorage` refuses to be made for a request without one, with a message that names the order (`django/contrib/messages/storage/session.py:SessionStorage.__init__`).
